name: Ankle Dorsiflexion
definition: A strict ankle-dorsiflexion isolation: either seated unilateral open-chain lifting against a band affixed to a foot board, or bilateral wall-supported lifting of the forefeet with both heels planted on the floor. The band fixture retains its individualized physical dorsiflexion stop and sole-to-board return. The wall fixture holds the back against the wall and the knees extended while the feet pivot about their grounded heels. Tibialis anterior is primary; the grouped long toe extensors are secondary dorsiflexion synergists. Their role transfers categorically from existing anatomical capabilities and resisted isometric dorsiflexion evidence to these dynamic fixtures; it is not a measured recruitment ranking or hypertrophy claim. This supersedes the initial exclusion based solely on the band study not measuring the toe extensors. Fibularis tertius remains outside this focused role expansion. Inversion, eversion, and deliberate toe extension are excluded as prime actions. Blood-flow-restricted, bilateral band, unsupported standing, unilateral wall, cable, machine, plate-loaded, manual-resistance, isometric, walking, balance, frontal-plane ankle, and deliberate toe-extension variants remain outside this contract.

variantAxes.description: Whether the whole foot moves freely against a band (open) or the forefoot moves while the heel stays grounded (heelSupported). Heel support is explicit rather than mislabeled as a freely moving foot.
The whole-body posture of the reviewed fixture.
The seat supporting the athlete while the foot moves against the band.
Whether knee motion creates the repetition; the study measured each participant's selected knee angle to reproduce the same posture between sessions but did not report one universal angle.
The held knee posture: self-selected for the band fixture, extended for the wall-supported heel pivot.
The dynamic ankle action creating the concentric repetition.
The bottom position: individual resting sole-to-board contact for the band, or sole-on-floor for the wall raise.
The band uses an individualized physical stop; the wall raise ends at comfortable dorsiflexion without lifting the heels.
The segment whose lower-leg-relative motion defines the repetition.
The study-defined bottom condition: the foot returns until the sole contacts the board before the next concentric phase.
The resistance interface: foot beneath the band, or grounded heels during the supported bodyweight pivot; no numerical bodyweight fraction is inferred.
Band anchored to the foot board, or both heels grounded ahead of a wall-supported torso.
Whether rails or a lever constrain the external-load path; a band affixed to a board does not create a fixed path.
Whether another lower-body joint propels the movement rather than the named isolated ankle action.
Posterior torso support required by the wall-raise fixture.
Both heels stay on the floor through the entire wall-supported repetition.

exerciseRules.description: Keep Seated Band Ankle Dorsiflexion geometry and support distinct from the other dorsiflexion fixture.
Keep Wall-Supported Tibialis Raise geometry and support distinct from the other dorsiflexion fixture.

execution.startingPosition: Sit comfortably with the working foot resting on a board beneath an elastic band affixed to that board. Set a physical stop where the working foot reaches its comfortable lifted position. Begin from the self-selected resting position with the sole on the board.
execution.movement: Lift the front of the foot toward the shin until it reaches the stop, without turning the foot inward or outward or lifting through the toes alone.
execution.endpoint: End the lift when the foot reaches the physical stop.
execution.returnPhase: Return under control until the sole touches the board.
execution.controlledJoints: Hold the selected knee posture still.
execution.supportAndPosture: Stay seated and supported by the seat while only the working foot moves.
disqualifyingCompensations: Bending or straightening the knee to swing the foot up turns the ankle lift into a leg swing.
Turning the foot inward or outward turns the ankle lift into a twisting foot movement.
Lifting through the toes alone turns the ankle lift into a toe raise.
execution.sideOrDirection: Complete every repetition before changing sides, then repeat with the other foot.

execution.startingPosition: Stand with your back against a wall and both feet flat on the floor ahead of you. Keep your knees straight and choose a foot position that lets you lift both forefeet while your heels stay planted.
execution.movement: Lift the fronts of both feet toward your shins, pivoting about your heels. Keep the feet pointing forward rather than turning inward or outward.
execution.endpoint: Stop at your comfortable lifted position while both heels remain on the floor.
execution.returnPhase: Lower both forefeet under control until the soles rest on the floor.
execution.controlledJoints: Hold the knees straight and move at the ankles; avoid lifting only the toes.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep your back against the wall and both heels planted throughout the set.
disqualifyingCompensations: Lifting the heels changes the movement into a calf raise.
Bending the knees or bouncing the body replaces the controlled ankle lift.
Extending only the toes without lifting the forefeet changes the movement into toe extension.
